newsitem.title: UK: Gen Accident says buys Sabre Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Gen Accident says buys Sabre Insurance.

text.p: UK-based composite insurer General Accident said on Thursday it is to buy Sabre Insurance, a company which specialises in insuring non-standard motor risks like young drivers, high performance cars and those with drink drive convictions.

The company declined to say how much it is to pay for niche market operator Sabre, which last year reported premium income of 30.9 million stg and pre-tax profits of 4.1 million. But analysts believe Sabre could be worth about 20 million stg.

"This move complements our existing capabilities in the UK market, and is in line with our strategic objective of further developing our successful UK general insurance business," said GA's general manager of UK personal lines business Bob Newton.
"Not only will it allow GA to develop its non-standard motor insurance capability, but GA will be able to facilitate growth for Sabre which would otherwise have been beyond their reach."
Shares in GA were 5-1/2 pence up at 730-1/2p by 1139 GMT.
Newton will become a board member of Sabre and Alan Turner, chairman and chief executive of Sabre, will join GA's senior management team. Sabre itself will operate autonomously in GA.

The composite does not plan to cut any of the 116 jobs at Sabre, which was formed in 1991 and has more than 100,000 policies in force across the United Kingdom. GA, which is one hundred years old this year, has 700,000 live UK motor policies.

GA is buying Sabre from the home-grown non-quoted Alan Turner Group, set up by its chief executive in 1982. Sabre was founded with the help of venture capitalists and its senior management are expected to benefit from the sale to GA.
The deal does not affect Alan Turner Group's broking interests.
